title: Federated ADMM from Bayesian Duality
claim: Standard primal-dual federated methods exchange point parameters and gradients; ours generalizes them by exchanging distributions and natural gradients.
layout: 2 panels, side-by-side, server-client message loops, red highlights marking changed quantities
description: Two side-by-side boxed panels titled 'ADMM' (left) and 'BayesADMM' (right) with an identical layout. Each has a rounded 'Server' box on the left and a rounded 'Client k' box on the right, joined by two curved arrows forming a loop. The top arrow runs from server to client and carries the global quantity. In ADMM this is θ_g, in black. In BayesADMM it is q_g, in red. The bottom arrow runs from client back to server. In ADMM it carries (θ_k, ∇ℓ_k), in black. In BayesADMM it carries (q_k, ∇̃E[ℓ_k]), in red. The parallel structure makes the red substitutions stand out: distributions replace point parameters, and natural gradients of expected losses replace gradients. The eye goes first to the red labels.
caption: In ADMM, the server broadcasts the global parameter $\vglobal$ to the clients who then update their local $\vparam_k$ and send them back to the server along with the gradients $\nabla \loss_k$ of their loss functions. Bayesian-ADMM {generalizes} ADMM by {using} distributions over global and local parameters (denoted by $\qglobal$ and $q_k$, respectively) and {replacing} gradients {by} natural gradients (denoted by \smash{$\natgrad \myexpect[\loss_k]$}).
abstract: We propose a new Bayesian approach to generalize the federated Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). We show that the solutions of variational-Bayesian (VB) objectives are associated with a duality structure that not only resembles the structure of ADMM's fixed-points but also generalizes it. For example, ADMM-like updates are recovered when the VB objective is optimized over the isotropic-Gaussian family, and new non-trivial extensions are obtained for other exponential-family distributions. These extensions include a Newton-like variant that converges in one step on quadratic objectives and an Adam-like variant that yields up to 7% accuracy boosts for deep heterogeneous cases. Our work opens a new Bayesian way to generalize ADMM and other primal-dual methods.
